author: Eustathius of Antioch
occasion: Eustathius writes to correct errors about Melchizedek, especially the view that he was greater than Christ or was the Holy Spirit, and to explain why Scripture calls him without father, without mother, and without genealogy.
argument: Eustathius argues that Melchizedek was a righteous human being, not a heavenly being, the Holy Spirit, or someone greater than Christ. He explains that Melchizedek is called without father, without mother, and without genealogy because Scripture deliberately omits his ancestry; the text reports an inference that this omission was due to his being a Canaanite from a cursed line, and Eustathius supports his Canaanite ethnicity from territorial evidence. The omission points readers to Christ, who is truly without father on earth according to the flesh and without mother in heaven according to his divinity. Melchizedek, moved by the prophetic Spirit, honored God with bread and wine, prefiguring the eternal offering Christ would make according to the order of Melchizedek rather than the bloody sacrifices of Aaron.

outline.move: Paul calls Melchizedek without mother and without father, and Eustathius explains that Melchizedek's genealogy is omitted because he was a Canaanite from a cursed line, unworthy ancestors for so righteous a man.

Eustathius confirms Melchizedek's Canaanite identity from territorial evidence; the section then includes material attributed to Chrysostom describing errors of the Melchizedekians and others who made him greater than Christ or identified him with the Holy Spirit.
Eustathius refutes the claim that Melchizedek was greater than Christ or the Holy Spirit, and explains that Scripture omitted his parents because he was a type bearing the image of Christ.

Eustathius shows how Melchizedek's lack of recorded beginning and end points to Christ's eternal existence, and how his offering of bread and wine prefigured Christ's eternal offering in place of the Aaronic bloody sacrifices.

cast.name: Melchizedek
cast.who: King of Salem and priest of God, presented as a righteous human type of Christ.

cast.name: Paul
cast.who: Apostle whose statement in Hebrews about Melchizedek being without father and mother frames the discussion.

cast.name: Christ
cast.who: The Son of God, the true eternal priest whom Melchizedek prefigured.

cast.name: Abraham
cast.who: Patriarch who lived near the oak of Mamre and encountered Melchizedek.

cast.name: Moses
cast.who: Lawgiver through whom genealogies were recorded.

cast.name: Adam
cast.who: First human, formed from the earth, contrasted with Melchizedek's unrecorded origin.

cast.name: Mary
cast.who: Virgin mother of Christ according to the flesh.

cast.name: David
cast.who: King from whose royal line Christ descended.

cast.name: Jesse
cast.who: Father of David, root from which Christ's human lineage springs.

cast.name: Solomon
cast.who: Son of David and Uriah's wife, cited as someone born of an illicit union yet genealogized.

cast.name: Abimelech
cast.who: Son of Gideon, cited as another person born of a harlot yet genealogized.

cast.name: Aaron
cast.who: Priest whose order offered bloody sacrifices of calves and lambs.

voices.speaker: Paul
voices.how_marked: Introduced as the one who 'expressed' Melchizedek as without mother and without father; his words are paraphrased rather than directly quoted.

voices.speaker: Chrysostom reporting Melchizedekian argument
voices.how_marked: Within Chrysostom's quotation, the Melchizedekian argument is introduced with φησίν.

voices.speaker: Chrysostom reporting other mistaken teachers
voices.how_marked: Within the same Chrysostom quotation, introduced with Ἄλλοι δὲ πλανηθέντες λέγουσιν.

voices.speaker: Jews
voices.how_marked: Introduced with 'Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν αὐτὸν εἰρήκασιν' (The Jews have said), reporting their claim that Melchizedek was born of a prostitute.

voices.speaker: An interlocutor
voices.how_marked: Introduced with 'ἀλλ' ἴσως τις ἐπερωτᾷ τῶν ἀκροατῶν καὶ λέγει' (But perhaps one of the hearers asks and says).

voices.speaker: God
voices.how_marked: Introduced with 'ὁ Θεὸς πρὸς τὸν μέλλοντα γεννᾶσθαι ἐκ τῆς παρθένου Μαρίας Ἰησοῦν ἐβόα λέγων' (God cried out to Jesus who was to be born of the virgin Mary, saying), followed by a quotation from Psalm 109.

key_terms.sense: Without mother; used of Melchizedek because Scripture records no mother for him, and applied to Christ in his heavenly divine existence.
Without father; used of Melchizedek because Scripture records no father, and applied to Christ in his earthly human existence.
Without genealogy; Scripture gives no ancestral line for Melchizedek, making him a type of Christ whose divine origin cannot be narrated.
A type or pattern; Melchizedek is a type of Christ, prefiguring him.
Image or likeness; Melchizedek bears the image of Christ, and humans were made according to God's image and likeness.
Order or rank; used of the priestly order of Melchizedek in contrast to the order of Aaron.
Priest; Melchizedek is called the greatest of priests, and Christ is priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
Offering; the offering Christ would make, prefigured by Melchizedek's offering of bread and wine.
Sacrifice; used of the bloody sacrifices of the Aaronic order, contrasted with the bread and wine offering.
Bloody sacrifice; the animal sacrifices of calves and lambs offered by the Aaronic priesthood.
Righteousness; Melchizedek is interpreted as 'king of righteousness' and is described as a righteous man.
Canaanite; Eustathius argues Melchizedek was of Canaanite descent, from a cursed line.
Melchizedekians; a heretical group who claimed Melchizedek was greater than Christ.
To trace a genealogy; Scripture genealogizes Christ according to the flesh but not Melchizedek.
Of like feelings or nature; Eustathius says Melchizedek was a human being with feelings like ours.

scripture: The author uses Septuagint book names and Psalm numbering. Psalm 109 in the Septuagint ('Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ') corresponds to Psalm 110 in modern Hebrew-based numbering. References to Hebrews should be cited as Hebrews. The oak of Mamre refers to Genesis 18:1. The bending of every knee alludes to Philippians 2:10. The phrase 'without father, without mother, without genealogy' comes from Hebrews 7:3.
uncertain: The exact date of the work is not stated in the source.
The original addressee or audience is not identified in the surviving fragments.
The precise extent of the original treatise is unknown, since only fragments survive.
Whether Eustathius himself wrote the section attributed to Chrysostom or it was inserted by a later compiler is not clear from the source.
Whether the material attributed to Chrysostom should be treated as part of Eustathius's own argument or as a separate catena insertion.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the text reports an inference that this omission was due to his being a Canaanite from a cursed line
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐκοῦν εἴποι τις ἂν τὸν Μελχισεδὲκ ἀγενεαλόγητον εἶναι διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ μηδὲ ὑπὸ Μωσέως γενεαλογεῖσθαι πώποτε, εἶναι δὲ Χαναναῖον τὸ γένος καὶ ἐκ τῆς ἐπαράτου ἐκείνης σπορᾶς ὁρμᾶσθαι, δίκαιον δὲ τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα καὶ οὐκ ἐκ προγόνων ὁρμώμενον δικαίων οὐδ' ἀπό τινος δικαίας σπορᾶς
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text presents the Canaanite-from-a-cursed-line explanation as something 'someone might say' (εἴποι τις ἂν), not as Eustathius's own inference. Eustathius then rejects the idea that Melchizedek's ancestors were unworthy, stating instead that Scripture deliberately omitted the genealogy because Melchizedek was a type of Christ.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Eustathius supports his Canaanite ethnicity from territorial evidence
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὅτι δὲ Χαναναῖος τὸ γένος δείκνυται ὁ Μελχισεδέκ, ἔστι δήπου τεκμήρασθαι καὶ ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἐκείνων ὧν ἐκράτει καὶ ἐβασίλευε κλιμάτων καὶ οἷς ἐπλησίαζεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Eustathius presents the Canaanite ethnicity as demonstrable from territorial evidence, but this appears in the section attributed to Chrysostom (marked by Τοῦ Χρυσοστόμου εἰς αὐτό), not in Eustathius's own voice. The brief should clarify that this argument comes from the Chrysostom quotation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Paul calls Melchizedek without mother and without father, and Eustathius explains that Melchizedek's genealogy is omitted because he was a Canaanite from a cursed line, unworthy ancestors for so righteous a man
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐκοῦν εἴποι τις ἂν... δίκαιον δὲ τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα... Οὐ θέμις οὖν ἦν γενεαλογεῖν... ∆ιὸ ἀπάτορα καὶ ἀμήτορά φησιν αὐτὸν εἶναι ἡ γραφή, οὐκ ἀξίους τοὺς προγόνους ἡγουμένη τῆς ἀρετῆς τοῦ δικαίου καὶ σώφρονος ἀνδρός
_unresolved_facts.fix: Paul calls Melchizedek without mother and without father, and Eustathius explains that Scripture deliberately omits Melchizedek's genealogy. The brief incorrectly attributes to Eustathius the view that the ancestors were 'unworthy'—this is presented as a hypothetical position (εἴποι τις ἂν) that Eustathius then modifies: Scripture omits the genealogy not because the ancestors were unworthy, but because Melchizedek was righteous in himself (καθ' ἑαυτὸν), and the omission serves to point to Christ.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the section then includes material attributed to Chrysostom describing errors of the Melchizedekians and others who made him greater than Christ or identified him with the Holy Spirit
_unresolved_facts.fix: The section includes material attributed to Chrysostom, but the Chrysostom material describes the errors of the Melchizedekians (who made him greater than Christ) and others (who identified him with the Holy Spirit). The brief's phrasing is accurate but should note that the Chrysostom material also contains the territorial argument for Canaanite identity and the comparison to Christ's own genealogy.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Chrysostom reporting Melchizedekian argument... introduced with φησίν
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Φιλονεικοῦντες οὖν καὶ βουλόμενοι δεῖξαι ὅτι μείζων ἐστὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ Μελχισεδὲκ προφέρουσιν ἡμῖν μάρτυρα τὴν γραφὴν λέγουσαν· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ. Πῶς γάρ, φησίν, οὐκ ἂν εἴη μείζων, οὗ κατὰ τὴν εἰκόνα καὶ τὴν τάξιν ἱερατεύει ὁ Χριστός;
_unresolved_facts.fix: The φησίν introduces the Melchizedekians' own rhetorical question ('How would he not be greater?'), not Chrysostom reporting their argument. The entire passage is Chrysostom describing the Melchizedekians' position, but the specific φησίν marks their direct speech within his report.

_unresolved_facts.claim: God... followed by a quotation from Psalm 109
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁ Θεὸς πρὸς τὸν μέλλοντα γεννᾶσθαι ἐκ τῆς παρθένου Μαρίας Ἰησοῦν ἐβόα λέγων· Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ
_unresolved_facts.fix: God is introduced as crying out to Jesus who was to be born, but the quotation that follows is from Psalm 109:4 LXX (Hebrews 7:17, 21). The brief should note that this is presented as God speaking prophetically to the pre-incarnate Christ about his future priesthood.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Abimelech... cited as another person born of a harlot yet genealogized
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: εὐθὺς ὁ Σολομῶν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου, εἶτα καὶ ὁ Ἀβιμέλεχ υἱὸς Γεδεών
_unresolved_facts.fix: Abimelech is cited, but the text does not explicitly state he was born of a harlot (πόρνης). The text only says Solomon was born 'of Uriah's [wife]' and Abimelech 'son of Gideon.' The Jewish claim about Melchizedek being born of a prostitute is what prompts the counterexample, but Abimelech's birth circumstances are not specified in the same way in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Aaron... Priest whose order offered bloody sacrifices of calves and lambs
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὐ κατὰ τὸν Ἀαρὼν τὸν ἐναίμοις θυσίαις λατρεύοντα
_unresolved_facts.fix: Aaron is described as 'serving with bloody sacrifices' (ἐναίμοις θυσίαις λατρεύοντα), but the specific animals 'calves and lambs' (μόσχους καὶ ἀμνούς) are mentioned earlier as what the Jewish synagogue offered, not specifically as Aaron's own offerings. The brief conflates the general description of Aaronic sacrifice with the specific animals listed.
